newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah steady at close, swaps biddish.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah steady at close, swaps biddish.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was steady against the dollar at close in slow trading on Friday.
Dealers said the market was squarish, with operators seen reluctant to make any move and trading trapped in a range between 2,600 and 2,630 level throughout the day.
"It's a dull day. We are staying mainly on the sidelines and waiting for the outcome of the central bankers meeting in Shanghai," one U.S. bank dealer said.
Spot rupiah ended at 2,610 at 0915 GMT against an opening of 2,601/09. The low was 2,625 and the high was 2,605.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,607.75/13.75 and 2,613.0/18.0, respectively.
The dealer said operators preferred to stay square ahead of the weekend and further uncertainty in the regional markets.
One Japanese bank dealer said sentiment appeared to be slightly better as the baht and the Singapore dollar were seen improving against the dollar.
"This morning we felt some attempts to push the rupiah below the 2,600 level. But there was not enough drive and the central bank was absent from the market," he said.
Dealers said the market remained cautious and sensitive to negative news. One said volatility would remain next week.
They said liquidity was a bit tight, with the central bank keeping short-term rates relatively expensive.
Overnight money was last at 14.0 percent.
"The central bank continues to keep short-term rates expensive to contain speculative dollar buying with cheap rupiah," one foreign bank dealer said.
The central bank kept its bilateral SBIs at 14.0 percent but raised one- and two-week money by 200 basis points to 10.0 and 10.5 percent respectively while keeping other rates unchanged.
The bank offered one-to-three-day SBIs at 14.0 percent, four-to-six day at 12.0 percent, one-month at 10.5, three at 11.0, six at 11.625 and one-year at 12.25 percent.
The local bank dealer said the central bank also scrapped the purchase of short-term papers (SBPUs), removing the chance for banks to seek liquidity from the central bank.
"We have to get funds from the market. The central bank is not taking any SBPUs today," she said.
Dealers said swaps remained biddish on fears that the central bank might further squeeze money market liquidity.
Overnight swap was at 1.30/1.45 and tom/next at 0.20/0.25.
One-month swap was at 21.0/22.0, two at 45.0/51.0, three at 67.0/70.0 and six at 120.0/124.0 points.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,378/2,682 but raised the conversion band to 2,592/2,640 on Friday from 2,566/2,614 on Thursday.
